chains.title: Alt allele strengthens TFAP2C binding at a TOX3 enhancer

links.claim: TFAP2C has its own QBiC-SELEX model in AP-2 group G030, and all four AP-2 models pass with positive alt effect; TFAP2C itself has z 10.07 with predicted_effect > 0 meaning alt binds more. However, no ENCODE TFAP2C ChIP-seq peak contains this variant in MCF7; absence is not definitive because there may be no TFAP2C experiment in that biosample.

The variant lies in the VEP-predicted enhancer ENSR16_9QTBS and 38 bp from the active dELS EH38E3180851, but no ENCODE cCRE directly overlaps the variant base, so the enhancer assignment is plausible but not fully resolved.

TOX3 is proposed as the target because it is the nearest protein-coding gene at 17.6 kb upstream and CASC16 is the local intronic transcript. There is no breast-tissue eQTL for this variant and no enhancer-promoter interaction evidence.
MCF7 is the DepMap expression context; TFAP2C is directly reported as expressed at 44.3 TPM in ACH-000019, so it is present in this breast cancer cell line.

TOX3 is a literature-supported breast cancer locus and 16q12 is a breast cancer risk region, but rs56007086 itself has no GWAS Catalog or Open Targets record and no breast-tissue eQTL, so the phenotype link is indirect.

predictions: Allele-specific TFAP2C ChIP-qPCR shows stronger TFAP2C binding to the alt allele at this element in MCF7 or another heterozygous breast cancer line.
An allele-specific TOX3 enhancer reporter shows higher activity from the alt allele in MCF7.
Mutation of the AP-2 motif abolishes the alt-allele reporter effect.
falsified_if: TFAP2C does not occupy this element in breast cancer cells.
The alt allele does not increase TOX3 reporter activity, or the effect is not AP-2-motif dependent.
TFAP2C knockdown does not reduce TOX3 expression from this locus.

chains.title: Alt allele strengthens PBX1 binding at a TOX3 enhancer

links.claim: PBX1 has its own QBiC-SELEX model in homeodomain group G274, with z 18.55 and effect 0.733, meaning alt binds more strongly. PBX1 is chosen because it has the own model and is expressed in the MCF7 context; PBX2-4 are only mapped in this group.
The variant is within the VEP enhancer ENSR16_9QTBS and near the active dELS EH38E3180851, making an enhancer mechanism plausible but not cCRE-confirmed at the variant base.
TOX3 is proposed as the target because it is the closest protein-coding gene at 17.6 kb upstream, with CASC16 also present; there is no breast eQTL and no demonstrated enhancer-promoter interaction.
MCF7 expresses PBX1 at 53.19 TPM in the ACH-000019 expression context, so PBX1 is present in the relevant breast cancer cell line.
TOX3 is a known breast cancer locus, so alt-enhanced PBX1 binding could increase TOX3 and contribute to 16q12 risk, but rs56007086 itself has no GWAS or Open Targets record and no breast eQTL.

predictions: PBX1 ChIP-qPCR or allelic imbalance assays show stronger PBX1 binding to the alt allele.
Mutation of the homeodomain motif reduces the allele-specific enhancer activity.
PBX1 knockdown lowers TOX3 expression in MCF7.
falsified_if: PBX1 does not occupy the element in breast cancer cells.
The homeodomain motif is dispensable for the allele effect.
PBX1 knockdown does not change TOX3 expression.

chains.title: Alt allele weakens ZNF395 binding and may derepress TOX3

links.claim: ZNF395 has its own QBiC-SELEX model in group G504 and binds the ref allele more strongly: z -53.42 with effect -0.776, meaning alt binds less. This is the strongest QBiC group shown, but ZNF395 is expressed at only 4.59 TPM in MCF7, so cellular relevance is weak.
The variant lies in the VEP-predicted ENSR16_9QTBS enhancer and 38 bp from an active dELS; no ENCODE cCRE directly overlaps the variant, so the element call is inferred.
The element is proposed to regulate TOX3 by proximity at 17.6 kb upstream, with CASC16 at the locus; there is no breast eQTL for the variant and no demonstrated ZNF395 regulation of TOX3.
MCF7 is the expression context and expresses ZNF395 at 4.59 TPM, low but detectable; this limits confidence in a ZNF395-driven mechanism in this cell line.

If ZNF395 represses TOX3, loss of ZNF395 binding on the alt allele could increase TOX3 and contribute to the 16q12 phenotype, but ZNF395 repressor activity on TOX3 is unproven and rs56007086 has no variant-specific association or breast eQTL.

predictions: ZNF395 ChIP-qPCR shows stronger binding to the ref allele at this element.
If ZNF395 is a repressor, the alt allele increases TOX3 expression and ZNF395 knockdown increases TOX3.
The allele effect depends on the ZNF395 motif.
falsified_if: ZNF395 does not bind the element in breast cancer cells.
ZNF395 knockdown does not change TOX3 expression.
The alt allele decreases rather than increases TOX3, or ZNF395 acts as an activator rather than a repressor.

chains.title: Alt allele strengthens ELF1 binding at a TOX3 enhancer

links.claim: ELF1 has its own QBiC-SELEX model and is a passing member of ETS group G003 with positive alt effect z 4.97, meaning alt binds more. This is weak because the leading ETV5 model has the opposite sign and ETS group members disagree on direction; ELF1 is chosen because it is a high-expression passing ETS member in MCF7.
The variant is in the VEP-predicted ENSR16_9QTBS enhancer and close to an active dELS, though no ENCODE cCRE directly overlaps the variant base.
TOX3 is proposed by proximity at 17.6 kb upstream, with CASC16 also in the immediate locus; there is no breast-tissue eQTL for the variant and no direct enhancer-to-TOX3 evidence.
MCF7 is the expression context and expresses ELF1 at 57.44 TPM, supporting ELF1 as a candidate ETS factor in this breast cancer line.
TOX3 is repeatedly implicated in breast cancer, so an ELF1-driven increase in TOX3 could contribute to the 16q12 signal, but rs56007086 has no variant-specific association record and no breast eQTL.

next_experiment: The cheapest experiment that separates the top two chains is an allele-specific reporter assay of the rs56007086-containing element (ref vs alt) in MCF7, with and without mutation of the AP-2 motif. It is cheaper and faster than allele-specific ChIP and directly tests whether the alt allele increases enhancer activity through the TFAP2C/AP-2 motif: the null predicts no alt-versus-ref difference, whereas the TFAP2C chain predicts an alt-dependent increase that is abolished by AP-2 motif mutation.
